newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weekly German intervention grain offers detailed.
newsitem.headline: Weekly German intervention grain offers detailed.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season continued to lag behind those in the same 1995/96 period, figures from the state grain intervention board BLE showed.
Volumes on Feb 7 totalled 514,019 tonnes compared with 1,379,195 tonnes a year earlier.
The figures describe volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores by the close last Friday.
Feed rye and and barley were being offered increasingly as ample feed wheat supplies dominated the feed grain market and pressurised the prices of other cereals, traders said.
Free market bread wheat and rye prices held up above the February intervention buying-in price of 241.52 marks a tonne.
